summary: Announces which link numbers may be used on the ARPANET. Link numbers 2 through 71 can be used for connections, 0 is the control link, others are reserved, and 191 is for measurement work. It updates RFC 107 and was written into the Host-Host protocol document.

eli5.summary: A list of which numbered lanes cars may use. Most lanes are open, one is for the control tower, and one is saved for measuring the traffic.

subtitle: A short announcement of which Host-Host link numbers may be used for connections.

tldr.problem: The Host-Host Protocol needed a clear statement of which link numbers hosts may use.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC announces that link numbers 2 through 71 (decimal) are valid for connections, and lists the other numbers as the control link, reserved, measurement or private experimental.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 107 and the same table was to appear as a declarative specification in the Host-Host Protocol document then being written.

today: RFC 179 updates RFC 107. The metadata lists its status as Unknown and no later RFC as replacing it.

sections.title: The Announcement
sections.content: Alex McKenzie of BBN writes that Steve Crocker asked him to announce that from now on link numbers 2-71 (decimal), inclusive, are valid for use in connections. The Host-Host Protocol Document he was writing would contain the assignments below as a declarative specification.
sections.eli5: Someone in charge said which numbered lanes can be used, and it will go in the rulebook.

sections.title: The Link Number Table
sections.content:
Link 0 is the control link. Links 2 through 71 are available for connections. Link 1 and links 72 through 190 are reserved and not for current use.

Link 191 is to be used only for measurement work under the direction of the Network Measurement Center at UCLA. Links 192 through 255 are available for private experimental use.
sections.eli5: Lane 0 is for control, lanes 2 to 71 are for everyone, a special lane is for measuring, and the highest lanes are for private tests.

sections.title: Relation to Other RFCs
sections.content: The memo lists RFC 107 as updated and is only one page long. It contains no further rationale; it simply states the assignment so implementers could rely on it.
sections.eli5: This note is a short update to an earlier rulebook page.

items.label: Measurement
